Cmshing and Grinding: The big stones of ore are crushed into small pieces with the help of jaw The crushed ore is then grinded with the help of ball mill or stamp mills to form h'der. This process is called crushing and grinding. ure -Oncentration of ores: The ores are obtained from the earth crust, these are generally associated is large number of impurities like sand, limestone, quartz, silicates etc. These impurities are gangue or matrix. The removal of impurities from the powdered ore and increased the of metal is known as concentration. The concentration of ore can be done by the "(Owing ways depending upon the nature of the ores.

300 A Complete NEB SolutJon to Chemistry - XI Gravity separation method: This method is based on the difference in densities of the ore i. particles and impurities. The powered ore is agitated with a running stream Of water. The heavier ore particles are settle down at the bottom, while the lighter impurities are Washed away with water. Generally, oxide and carbonate ores are concentrated by this method Magnetic separation method: This method is based on the nature Of ores i.e. ore or the impurities are magnetic in nature. The two can be separated from each other by means of magnetic separators.

Froth floatation method: This method is suitable for sulphide ore of metal. The process is based iii. on the different wetting properties of ore and gangue particle with water and pine oil. Ore is wetted with oil and impurities are wetted with water.

Calcination and roasting: Calcination is a process in which ore is heated in the absence of air c. below their melting point. During calcinations: (i) mass becomes porous (ii) volatile impurities are removed (iii) carbonates ore decompose to oxides. Example:

During roasting (i) sulphide ores are generally converted into oxides (ii) volatile impurities are removed (iii) free S, As and Sb are removed as SOD As-z03 and Sb203 respectively.

Example: 2ZnS + 302 2ZnO + 302 Cus + 202 ——-..-...-..+ CuS04 Reduction by carbon (Smelting): The oxides of less electropositive metals like P b, Zn,FeSn,Cu etc are reduced by strongly heating them with coal or coke. Reduction of oxide with carbon at high temperature is known as smelting. Here, the calcinated or roasted ore is mixed with coal or coke and flux and heated in a reverberatory furnace or blast furnace in the presence of air.

The nature of the flux used depends upon the nature of the impurity to be removed.

Liquation process: This process is used when the impurity is less fusible than the metal i.
The impure metal is heated on the sloping hearth of a furnace.

Distillation process: This process is used for the purification of volatile metals like Hg, Cd' etc. The crude metal is heated in a retort and its vapours are separately condensed in a receiver• Electro-refining: Highly electropositive metal like Al, Cu, Ag, Zn, Sn, etc. are refined by iii. method. The impure metal is made as anode while the pure metal is made as cathode in the the electrolytic cell. A solution of a soluble salt of the metal is used as electrolyte. On passing electricity, positive charge metal ion is deposited at cathode.
